<p class="eyebrow">Spatially aware NMF for integral-field spectroscopy</p>

# Recover component spectra and spatial structure from IFU cubes

<p class="hero-copy">
SpaxNMF fits non-negative component spectra together with component-weight
maps, combining smooth spectral regularization, Gaussian spatial coupling, and
optional sparse priors for compact sources.
</p>

<div class="hero-actions">
  <a class="hero-button hero-primary" href="getting-started.html">Get Started</a>
  <a class="hero-button hero-secondary" href="model.html">See the Equations</a>
</div>
</div>

<div class="hero-card">
<h3>Implemented objective</h3>

$$
\mathcal{L}(A,S)=
\|X-AS\|_F^2
+\lambda_S \|DS\|_F^2
+\sum_c \lambda_{A,c}\sum_{i,j} w_{ij}(A_{ic}-A_{jc})^2
+\sum_c \lambda_{C,c}\|A_{:,c}\|_1
$$

<p>
<code>A</code> contains component weights, not chemical abundances. The spatial
term regularizes those weights across neighboring spaxels through
Gaussian kernel weights <code>w<sub>ij</sub></code>.
</p>
</div>
</div>
:::

<div class="feature-card">
<h3>Interpretability first</h3>
<p>
The factorization is non-negative, so each spaxel is reconstructed as a
positive combination of shared component spectra and spatially varying
component weights.
</p>
</div>
<div class="feature-card">
<h3>Designed for real cubes</h3>
<p>
The package includes helpers for IFU reshaping, metadata preservation, and
comparative diagnostics against PCA and vanilla NMF on the same target.
</p>
</div>
<div class="feature-card">
<h3>Method development ready</h3>
<p>
The current implementation supports smooth spectra, weighted spatial priors,
and sparse compact-source components inside the same torch optimization loop.
</p>
</div>

## Core Factorization

<div class="two-up">
<div class="equation-panel">
<p class="section-kicker">Factorization</p>
<h3>Shared spectra, spatially varying weights</h3>

$$
X \approx AS
$$

<p>
<code>X</code> is the spaxel-by-wavelength matrix, <code>A</code> is the
component-weight matrix, and <code>S</code> contains the component spectra.
</p>
</div>

<div class="equation-panel">
<p class="section-kicker">Spatial term</p>
<h3>Weighted coherence between neighboring spaxels</h3>

$$
w_{ij} = \exp\left(-\frac{d_{ij}^2}{2\sigma^2}\right)
$$

<p>
This term discourages noisy salt-and-pepper maps by penalizing strong changes
between nearby component weights while allowing distant spaxels to decouple.
</p>
</div>
</div>

## Quick Workflow

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["IFU cube<br/>nx × ny × nλ"] --> B["cube_to_matrix()"]
  B --> C["spaxel × wavelength matrix X"]
  C --> D["spax_nmf()"]
  D --> E["component-weight maps A"]
  D --> F["component spectra S"]
  D --> G["reconstruction AS"]
  E --> H["component_map()"]
  F --> I["plot(type = 'spectra')"]
  G --> J["predict(type = 'cube') / fitted()"]
```

## Main Entry Points

<div class="info-grid">
<div class="info-panel">
<h3>Fit models</h3>
<p><code>spax_nmf()</code> fits the torch model and returns spectra, weights,
reconstructions, and optimization history.</p>
</div>

<div class="info-panel">
<h3>Reshape data</h3>
<p><code>cube_to_matrix()</code> and <code>matrix_to_cube()</code> move between
IFU cubes and the matrix view required by the optimizer.</p>
</div>

<div class="info-panel">
<h3>Inspect results</h3>
<p><code>component_map()</code>, <code>component_spectrum()</code>,
<code>plot()</code>, and <code>plot_reconstruction()</code> provide quick
diagnostics.</p>
</div>

<div class="info-panel">
<h3>Benchmark on real targets</h3>
<p>The benchmark page shows how the current model behaves on a mixed
galaxy+GC+sky cube under matched preprocessing.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("RafaelSdeSouza/SpaxNMF")
```

`torch` must be available in the local R installation.
